definitions: In conclusion; giving a brief summary of the main points covered.
A summary or concise statement of points made in discussion.
examples: To sum up, our new strategy will focus on sustainability.
To sum up, we must focus our efforts on sustainability.

definitions: Taking all factors, circumstances, and details into account overall.
everything considered, taking every factor or circumstance into consideration
taking every factor, event, or circumstance into complete consideration before forming judgment
taking all relevant facts and aspects into account before reaching a final decision
examples: All things considered, the event went remarkably well for everyone.
When all things were considered, the regional expansion plan was declared a commercial success.
All things considered, the international cultural exchange program was deemed a great success.
When all options were considered, renewing the lease proved to be most economical.

definitions: Used to express conditionality in polite or formal register requests.
Past tense auxiliary used in polite indirect inquiries and phrasing.
Feeling curiosity or introducing a polite indirect request to someone.
examples: I was wondering if you could spare a few minutes today.
I was wondering if you had time to review my draft.
I was wondering whether you could help me move this box.

definitions: A polite word used in formal requests and expressions gratitude.
examples: Would you be so kind as to send me the report?

definitions: To express regret or ask pardon for a fault or offense.
examples: I sincerely apologise for the delay in responding to your email.

definitions: Used as a polite auxiliary verb to make requests or suggestions.
examples: Could you please provide more details regarding the upcoming schedule?

definitions: In fundamental respects; fundamentally or used to summarize informally.
examples: Basically, we need to double our sales before the quarter ends.

definitions: In essence; at the most basic or fundamental level.
examples: The two proposals are essentially the same despite minor wording differences.

definitions: Informal spoken contraction of going to, used in informal register.
examples: We are gonna catch the early movie at the cinema tonight.

definitions: Informal spoken contraction of want to, used in casual conversation.
examples: Do you wanna grab a quick bite to eat after work?

definitions: In support of or approving of a particular proposal or plan.
examples: The majority of council members voted in favor of the proposal.

definitions: Considering both supporting arguments and opposing objections to an idea.
examples: We debated the arguments for and against building a new airport.

definitions: The set of reasons or arguments supporting a particular course action.
examples: The professor presented the case for investing in solar power.

definitions: The arguments, evidence, or reasons opposing a specific action plan.
examples: The lawyer carefully laid out the case against the accused defendant.

definitions: Used to introduce factual evidence established by formal scientific studies.
examples: Research shows that regular physical exercise improves sleep quality significantly.

definitions: As stated by or in conformity with a specific authority source.
examples: According to the weather forecast, it will rain heavily tomorrow afternoon.

definitions: Providing agreement, backing, or approval for a person or cause.
examples: Citizens gathered in the town square in support of clean energy.

definitions: Used to introduce an example that explains or clarifies a statement.
examples: To illustrate my point, consider the results of last year's survey.

definitions: As an example; used to illustrate a general statement made.
examples: Many green vegetables, for instance spinach, are high in iron.

definitions: Used to explain a point more clearly or remove confusion.
examples: To clarify, the deadline has been moved to next Friday afternoon.

definitions: Used to introduce a brief recap of the main points discussed.
examples: To summarize, our main goals are reducing costs and increasing quality.

definitions: Used to introduce final remarks or a summary of writing.
examples: In conclusion, sustainable practices benefit both the environment and economy.

definitions: Considering all relevant facts, details, and circumstances before judging.
examples: Taking everything into account, the event was a complete success.

definitions: Based on a calculated mean; usually or typically in general cases.
examples: On average, employees spend two hours commuting to work every day.

definitions: A large or important quantity of people, items, or objects.
examples: A significant number of students chose to study abroad this year.

definitions: A minor proportion or fraction of a total amount.
examples: Only a small percentage of applicants passed the difficult entrance exam.

definitions: The greater number or part of a group; more than half.
examples: The majority of voters supported the new environmental protection law.

definitions: The smaller number or part, especially a number less than half.
examples: Only a minority of citizens disagreed with the proposed budget changes.

definitions: Numerical data demonstrates or proves a particular fact or trend clearly.
examples: Recent statistics show that crime rates have decreased significantly this year.

definitions: Collected information points toward or indicates a likely conclusion or trend.
examples: Scientific data suggests that global temperatures will continue to rise steadily.

definitions: As indicated or reported by a structured study of people's opinions.
examples: According to a survey, most citizens prefer working flexible weekly hours.

definitions: Used to introduce a calculated rough value, total, or approximate figure.
examples: It is estimated that millions of tourists visit Paris every year.

definitions: Almost fifty percent of a total group, number, or quantity.
examples: Nearly half of all respondents answered all survey questions completely.

definitions: A quantity exceeding fifty percent of a total population or group.
examples: More than half the workforce voted in favor of the contract.

definitions: An amount smaller than twenty-five percent of a total whole.
examples: Less than a quarter of the budget was spent on advertising.

definitions: Twice as much in quantity, size, degree, or value recorded.
examples: The new factory produced double the amount of goods this year.

definitions: A sudden, large, and rapid rise in numbers or price.
examples: There was a sharp increase in fuel prices following the storm.

definitions: A minor, small, or subtle drop in quantity or degree.
examples: The report noted a slight decrease in overall electricity consumption yesterday.

definitions: A continuous, regular, and predictable increase over a period of time.
examples: We observed a steady rise in online sales over the year.
